intro: Walk down a shopping strip in almost any Illinois town and you may pass a dojo, a dojang and a boxing gym. Across the road, a public high school has its own wrestling room. Each room has a different owner, a different source of money and a different set of rules.

The names on those doors came from far away. Dojo is Japanese, dojang is Korean, kwoon is Cantonese and gym is Greek. Many of these arts reached Illinois only when laws let their teachers come. The Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882, the quotas of 1924, the camps of 1942 and the new immigration law of 1965 all shaped who arrived in Chicago, and when.

In this unit, you will compare who owns, pays for and governs four kinds of rooms. You will read laws, reports and street records. You will explain how immigration history is written on the signs of Chicago neighborhoods.
bigQuestion: How did laws about schools, business and immigration shape the martial arts rooms of Illinois?

choices: a Korean word for a taekwondo room
test.why: Dojang is the Korean reading of the characters for a place of the way.

test.q: Who pays for a public school wrestling room?
choices: mostly local taxes and state money
test.why: Public schools are paid for mostly by property taxes and state money.

test.q: Which group runs state tournaments for Illinois high schools?
test.why: The IHSA runs state tournaments and sets season dates.

test.q: Which 1973 law protects students with disabilities in federally funded programs?
test.why: Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 bans disability discrimination.

test.q: Which city was home to Robert Trias's 1946 karate school?
test.why: Trias opened his school in Phoenix, Arizona, in 1946.

test.q: What kind of event was the 1964 Long Beach championship?
choices: an open tournament for many styles
test.why: Long Beach was an open tournament where many styles competed.

test.q: What sets fees and ranks at a storefront karate school?
test.why: A storefront school is a private business that sets its own fees and ranks.

test.q: Why is college judo usually a club sport?
choices: The NCAA holds no judo championship
test.why: Without an NCAA championship, most colleges run judo as a student club.

test.q: Which Illinois office licenses professional boxers?
choices: the Department of Financial and Professional Regulation
test.why: The Department of Financial and Professional Regulation licenses pro boxers and promoters.

test.q: What did the Magnuson Act of 1943 do?
choices: repealed Chinese exclusion with a small quota
test.why: The Magnuson Act repealed exclusion and set a quota of 105 a year.

test.q: What stands on Wentworth Avenue and is now the Pui Tak Center?
choices: the old On Leong Merchants Association building
test.why: The late-1920s On Leong building is now the Pui Tak Center.

test.q: About what share of the people removed in 1942 were American citizens?
test.why: About two-thirds of the roughly 120,000 people removed were U.S. citizens.

test.q: What did the 1983 report Personal Justice Denied conclude?
choices: The removal was not justified by military need
test.why: The commission found the removal was not justified by military need.

test.q: Which law ended national origins quotas?
choices: the Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965
test.why: The 1965 act, signed by President Johnson, ended the 1924 quota system.

test.q: Where did a Korean business district grow in Chicago after 1965?
choices: along Lawrence Avenue in Albany Park
test.why: Korean churches, stores and dojang opened along Lawrence Avenue in Albany Park.

write.prompt: Pick one Illinois martial arts room: a school wrestling room, a storefront dojo or dojang, a college judo club, a boxing gym or a lion dance hall. Argue what shaped it most: a school rule, a business need or an immigration law. Cite two or three records from this unit, such as Title IX (1972) or the 1965 immigration act, and explain what each did.
tips: Name each law or record and give its year.
Say who owns the room, who pays for it and who writes its rules.
Attribute customs to the community that keeps them.
Compare two rooms rather than ranking one above another.
Use terms from the unit, such as license, quota and national governing body.
